sentences.text: The genus name Kuszholia means "Milky Way bird," derived from the Kazakh term for the Milky Way, and the fossils consist of vertebrae from an animal estimated to be chicken-sized.

Fossils of Kuszholia were discovered in the Bissekty Formation within the Kyzyl Kum desert of Bukhara Province, Uzbekistan, and were described by Russian paleontologist Lev Alexandrovich Nesov in 1992.

While some suggest Kuszholia were coelurosaurs near the ancestry of birds, most scientists classify them as avialans, specifically primitive ornithurans or enantiornithines. The genus contains only a single species, Kuszholia mengi, and is classified within the parent group Ornithurae. Kuszholia has been placed in the clade Patagopterygiformes, with a separate family, Kuszholiidae, erected for the genus. The Spanish taxobox lists the unranked family as Enantiornithes.

Kuszholia lived during the Coniacian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 89.8 and 86.3 million years ago, though the Paleobiology Database records the time range as the Turonian, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
